He drives about 97% of the results of the equations and leaves the remainder as exercises, which I believe is very effective for reinforcing students' understanding. This approach encourages us not to simply accept results but to follow the derivations and accompanying assumptions step by step in a detailed manner.

The curriculum is also well-structured. In other words, one can easily follow and even anticipate the upcoming topics based on the current discussion. Personally, I never had difficulty keeping up or felt confused about how a topic was connected to the overall discussion.

Finally, he encourages student participation as much as possible. Considering the small class size (about 10 people), a significant portion of the class is dedicated to discussing the brilliant questions raised by students. The goal is not necessarily to provide a perfect answer, since the discussions often delve deeply and would require considerable study on their own, but to understand the concepts together and gain insights from different perspectives. Sometimes this even leads to asking deeper and more meaningful questions. This level of student engagement, which I greatly appreciated, is something I haven’t encountered in any other class. Therefore, I’m very glad I took this course and I truly hope that its continuation will be offered next year. (I would love to take it.)
